console-ground.purpose: Page background — the darkest layer of the console in dark theme; cool paper in light theme.

panel-surface.purpose: Cards, popovers, dialogs — one step above the ground.

rail-surface.purpose: Sidebar rail — one step below the ground so navigation recedes.

charcoal-surface.purpose: Muted fills — secondary buttons, hover washes, segmented-control troughs, skeletons.

slate-label.purpose: Secondary text — captions, units, table headers, context lines.

signal-teal.purpose: The single interactive accent — primary buttons, focus rings, active nav, brand mark, chart series 1.

teal-ink.purpose: Deep navy label on Signal Teal fills (primary button text, brand waveform).

health-green.purpose: Binding status lamp: healthy machines, resolved anomalies, positive deltas. Never decoration.

alert-amber.purpose: Binding status lamp: warning machines, warn threshold rules/bands, warning-severity anomalies.

critical-red.purpose: Binding status lamp: critical machines, crit threshold rules/bands, open critical anomalies, destructive actions.

badge-critical-fill.purpose: Solid red behind white count-badge digits in both themes so they clear 4.5:1.

info-cyan.purpose: Neutral-informational states (Acknowledged anomaly status), chart series 2. Never a machine-health meaning.

plot-violet.purpose: Chart series 3 only — keeps multi-series plots separable without borrowing status hues.

hairline.purpose: The 1px borders and dividers that separate every surface — the system's only elevation language.

display.purpose: Summary metric values in the six-cell strip — the largest numbers on the page. Always tabular.

body.purpose: Default UI copy, table cells, list rows, form values.

label.purpose: Metric-cell captions, table headers, chips, context lines — often in Slate Label color.

mono.purpose: Machine identifiers (P-101, M-204) in tables, selects, command palette, chart footers.

shadows.name: active-segment
shadows.purpose: Tailwind shadow-sm on the selected cell of period/metric segmented controls — a 1px lift confirming the pressed cell. The only shadow on content chrome.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Tailwind shadow-md on popovers, selects, dropdown menus, chart tooltips.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Tailwind shadow-lg on side sheets and dialogs.

shadows.name: inset-rail
shadows.purpose: Tailwind shadow-sm on the content card of the inset sidebar variant, separating content column from rail on wide screens.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default Tailwind transition-* duration for hover/focus/active color changes on buttons, inputs, rows, nav items.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: duration-100 + tw-animate-css fade/zoom/slide for popovers, selects, dropdowns, sheets.

motion.name: rail-collapse
motion.purpose: Sidebar width/position collapse between expanded, icon-rail, and off-canvas states.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons press down 1px under the pointer; no scale or spring.

narrative.overview:
MechSense is a monitoring console judged on state readability first: the engineer opens the app and reads fleet condition in one glance. The Overview voice is instrument-panel precision — dense, tabular numerals, status-lamp color, and copy that reads like gauges and nameplates rather than marketing. It refuses the generic equal-size metric-card grid as its structure: health leads as a dense status table sorted problems-first, summary metrics support it, and the sensor trend with its threshold horizon closes the story.

The world is a deep navy/charcoal ground with a signal-teal accent, inherited from the Phase-1 tokens and pinned by the surface brief. Component philosophy is restrained and instrumental: hairline borders, flat surfaces, no lift or shadow on resting cards — states change color and value, never elevation. Amber and red are reserved for warning and critical machine meaning; they are status lamps, not decoration. Every number, chart, and threshold traces to real backend data (provenance over decoration).

Both themes ship: dark is the default at first paint; the light theme keeps the same hues as print-ink depths on cool paper. Responsive coverage is full — the side rail collapses to an icon rail and then a hamburger sheet, the metric strip reflows 6→3→2 columns, and the fleet table sheds columns on narrow widths.
keyCharacteristics: Instrument-panel precision: dense rhythm, tabular numerals, gauge-and-nameplate copy
Deep navy ground + signal-teal accent; amber/red strictly reserved for warning/critical
Flat and layered: 1px hairline borders are the only elevation on resting surfaces
Geist with tabular figures on every sensor readout, count, and table cell
Signature "Threshold horizon" charts: dashed warn/crit rules, tinted limit bands, anomaly interval shading
shadcn v4 grammar: small radii, restrained surfaces, color-only state changes

rules.name: The Status Latch Rule
rules.body: Green means healthy, amber means warning, red means critical — nothing else, ever. Amber and red are reserved for warning/critical machine meaning; they must never decorate headings, branding, or "positive" emphasis. If a color looks like a status lamp, it must report a status.

rules.name: The Teal Monopoly Rule
rules.body: Signal Teal is the only interactive accent. Status hues never fill a primary button; teal never fakes a status. Rarity is what makes the accent read as "action" against a field of lamps.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every sensor value, count, delta, threshold, and table cell renders with tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums). Columns of numbers must align like a gauge panel; proportional digits are a bug.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn, not cast. Every resting surface is defined by its 1px border and its step on the surface ladder; a shadow on a resting card is a violation. Shadows belong only to transient overlays and the active segment of a control.

dos: Do keep amber and red locked to warning/critical machine meaning — status chips, threshold rules, critical deltas, destructive actions only.
Do render every measured number with tabular numerals and its engineering unit (mm/s, °C, RPM, %, bar).
Do define resting surfaces with a 1px Hairline border and a step on the surface ladder (Rail → Ground → Panel).
Do draw every sensor chart as a Threshold horizon: dashed warn/crit rules, 7% tinted bands, and shaded anomaly intervals from real configured limits.
Do keep copy instrument-panel: nameplates, gauges, counts, and thresholds — no marketing tone.
Do give every data view real loading, error, and empty states inside the same framed panel.
Do sort fleet tables problems-first and keep the worst-condition machine as the default chart selection.
Do use Signal Teal as the sole interactive accent and draw focus as a 3px teal ring at 50% alpha.
donts: Don't put a drop-shadow on a resting card, panel, or table — depth is a 1px border, not a shadow.
Don't use amber, red, or green for decoration, branding, or generic emphasis.
Don't animate chart data draw-on or springy entrances — plots render instantly; motion is reserved for 150ms state transitions and 100ms overlay entrances.
Don't invent trend arrows, comparisons, or percentages that don't trace to backend data (provenance over decoration).
Don't use proportional digits in any sensor value, count, or table cell.
Don't make a filled primary button more than once per view; everything else is outline, ghost, or text.
Don't add a second accent hue outside the chart-series palette (teal, cyan, violet, amber, red).
